_meta.format: Matches MaterialProps in src/engine/acoustics/materials.ts: each material has `absorption` (8-band array) and `scattering` (8-band array). In materials.ts scattering is generated from a single mid-band value via scatterCurve(sMid); here we record that source value as `scattering_mid` so a reviewer can call scatterCurve(scattering_mid) when merging. The expanded 8-band `scattering` array shown is scatterCurve(scattering_mid) with shape [0.5,0.6,0.75,0.9,1.0,1.3,1.7,1.9].
_meta.band_mapping: Source tables give 6 octave bands [125,250,500,1000,2000,4000] (ASTM C423 / ISO 354) or pyroomacoustics 7-band [125..8000]. We map to our 8 bands by: 63 Hz = copy of 125 Hz (no measured data below 125 in standard tables); 8 kHz = copy of 4 kHz UNLESS the source is a pyroomacoustics 7-band entry that already includes 8 kHz (then we use it). This matches the existing convention documented at the top of materials.ts.

sources.pra: pyroomacoustics materials database (LCAV), https://github.com/LCAV/pyroomacoustics/blob/master/pyroomacoustics/data/materials.json — itself compiled from standard architectural-acoustics tables.
sources.cssbi: Canadian Sheet Steel Building Institute Facts 16-18, bare metal deck field data, https://www.agwaymetals.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/04/CSSBI-Facts16-18.pdf.
sources.snow: Buser/Ishida in-situ snow acoustics; J. Sound & Vibration 1991 (deep snow), summarised: alpha<0.4 below 1kHz, ~0.85 above. ESTIMATE fitted to that description.
sources.iso9613: ISO 9613-2 ground classes (porous/hard) used by analogy for outdoor surfaces, as in existing materials.ts.

wood_panel.notes: Thin wood paneling on studs: low-frequency panel resonance lifts the 63-250 Hz absorption. Warm, slightly bass-shy reflection.

plywood_thin.notes: Strong bass-trap behaviour (alpha 0.42 @125). Sounds boomy-room / drum-like vs solid wood. Distinct LOW-frequency cue.

wooden_door.notes: Solid, fairly reflective; nearly flat. Hard to distinguish from plaster by ear (see report).

sheet_metal.notes: Bare flat metal: very bright, near-mirror, slight panel ring at 125. Crisp metallic echo, very low scatter.

perforated_metal_absorber.notes: Helmholtz/porous absorber: kills lows-mids but REFLECTS highs (opposite tilt to carpet/foam). Unusual bright-but-dead character.

water.source: acoustic_supplies water surface [0.008,0.008,0.013,0.015,0.020,0.025] at [125..4000]. 63=125, 8k=4k. (Refines existing materials.ts 'water' estimate.)
water.notes: Near-perfect specular mirror, marginally absorptive at HF. Acoustically almost identical to marble/glazed tile.

marble.source: pra marble_floor + acoustic_supplies 'marble or glazed tile' [0.01,0.01,0.01,0.01,0.02,0.02]. 63=125,8k=4k. (Matches/confirms existing.)
marble.notes: Hardest reflector; flat near-zero absorption. The reference 'bright' surface.

ceramic_tile.notes: Acoustically indistinguishable from marble; differs only in scattering if grout/relief present.

plaster_smooth.notes: Hard, very slightly HF-absorbing. Close to existing 'plaster'.

plasterboard.notes: Drywall: panel resonance eats bass (0.29@125), bright above. Hollow-wall character vs solid plaster_smooth.

gypsum_acoustic_perforated.notes: Broadband absorber peaking at 500-1k. Mid-heavy dead sound.

acoustical_plaster.notes: Looks hard but is broadband-absorptive — deceptive surface, good 'trick' material for trainer.

drapes_heavy.notes: Pleated heavy fabric: high scatter (folds) + strong mid/HF absorption. Soft, diffuse, fuzzy reflection.

curtains_velvet.notes: Lighter absorber than drapes_heavy; lets more bass through. Similar timbre to existing 'curtain'.

panel_fabric_rockwool.notes: Near-total broadband absorber (anechoic-like). The 'deadest' material — no usable echo. Reference dead surface.

fiberglass_board.notes: Like acoustic_foam but passes more bass (0.18@125). Distinct only at low frequency from foam.

audience_seated.notes: Highly absorptive + highly diffuse (people-as-rough-surface). Could signal a crowded room.

ceiling_tile_fissured.notes: Suspended ceiling: broadband, rising-with-freq absorption. Typical office-ceiling cue.

snow_fresh.source: snow (ESTIMATE). Fitted to literature: alpha<0.4 below 1kHz rising to ~0.85-0.9 above 1kHz for high-porosity fresh snow. No standard ISO 354 row exists.
snow_fresh.notes: ESTIMATE. Behaves like a porous outdoor absorber — kills highs, passes some bass. The classic 'silent after snowfall' surface. High scatter (granular).

vegetation_dense.source: iso9613 (ESTIMATE by analogy to porous ground / existing 'grass', pushed higher for dense foliage). No single authoritative ISO 354 row.
vegetation_dense.notes: ESTIMATE. Anchored to existing 'grass' [0.1,0.2,0.35,0.5,0.6,0.65]; raised mid/HF absorption + very high scatter (leaves) for hedges/bushes.
